```{r data generation, echo = FALSE, results = "hide"}
n <- 10
p <- 0.30
x <- 4

correct <- round(dbinom(x, size = n, prob = p), 4)

opt2 <- round(pbinom(x, size = n, prob = p), 4)       # P(X ≤ 4)
opt3 <- round(1 - pbinom(x - 1, n, p), 4)            # P(X ≥ 4)
opt4 <- round(dbinom(x + 1, n, p), 4)                # P(X = 5)
opt5 <- round(pbinom(x - 1, n, p), 4)                # P(X ≤ 3)
opt6 <- round(1 - pbinom(x, n, p), 4)                # P(X > 4)
```

Question
========

A quality-control inspector examines 10 products. Each product has a probability of 0.30 of being defective, independently of the others.

Let $X$ denote the number of defective products.

What is the probability that **exactly 4 products are defective**?

Answerlist
----------

* `r sprintf("%.4f", correct)`
* `r sprintf("%.4f", opt2)`
* `r sprintf("%.4f", opt3)`
* `r sprintf("%.4f", opt4)`
* `r sprintf("%.4f", opt5)`
* `r sprintf("%.4f", opt6)`
